import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

<Aside type="note" title="Status: historical design record — superseded by the in-app Cupboard">
This page is the original design rationale for a standalone plugin marketplace.
The plugin **distribution** model it proposes (a `kind` discriminator on
`papercusp.json`, install-time capability consent, per-harness enable, the
`actions` primitive, lockfiles) has shipped — but the storefront is now the
**in-app Cupboard** (`apps/operator-public` = `@papercusp/cupboard-worker`, a
Cloudflare Worker + D1, live at `cupboard.papercusp.com`), not a
`papercuspai.com/marketplace/` site. The Cupboard is a single catalog with six
listing **kinds** — `harness` (join), `blueprint` (fork), `plugin` (install),
`pack` (install), `knowledge-pack` (install), and `template` (install) — exposed over HTTP at the
worker root: `/listings` (kind-aware) and `/harnesses` (the `kind='harness'`
view), with no `cupboard:*` MCP verbs. (The runtime-less code-tool pack is
`pack`; its interim `tool-pack` value still parses as an alias. The original
proposal's `snapshot` kind was **retired** —
`retire-snapshots-instance-spec-2026-06-09` D-005.) Plugins
install to `~/.papercusp/global-plugins/<slug>/`
and mount under `/api/plugins/<name>/`. Treat the URLs, package names
(`papercusp-marketplace`, `papercusp-plugin-sdk`), and `~/.papercusp/installed/`
paths below as the historical proposal's wording, not current identifiers; the
concepts map onto the Cupboard. Read this for the *why*; see the
[authoring quickstart](/internal/docs/spec/plugin-quickstart) for the *how* today.
</Aside>

## 14.0 Why this exists

The marketplace today distributes **harness templates** — reusable recipes
that spin up concrete harness instances (papercup-coding, papercup-org). They
ship with their own roles, model preferences, and project layout.

But templates can't share **integrations**. If `papercup-coding` wants
"one-click publish to Cloudflare Pages", that integration is either baked into
the template (forcing every coding harness in the world to know about
Cloudflare) or has to be implemented separately by every template author. Same
for vscode-server, Slack notifications, Postgres schema management, etc.

This is why every mature plugin ecosystem has a **plugin marketplace** distinct
from a **theme/template marketplace**: WordPress separates plugins from themes;
VS Code separates extensions from project templates; Backstage separates
plugins from app shells.

Papercusp needs the same split. Templates are recipes; plugins are horizontal
capabilities that any template can pull in.

## 14.1 Templates vs plugins — the ontological split

| | **Harness template** | **Plugin** |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | Recipe for spinning up a harness | Horizontal capability any harness can use |
| Cardinality | 1 template → N harness instances | 1 plugin install → mounted into N harness instances |
| Install scope | Per-instance (each `papercusp run` produces a fresh instance) | Per-machine (installed globally; enabled per harness instance) |
| Examples | papercup-coding, papercup-org, "research-org", "habit-tracker" | cloudflare-pages, vscode-server, slack-notifier, gemini-narrator |
| Composition | One template per harness | Multiple plugins per harness instance |
| Manifest field | `kind: 'template'` | `kind: 'plugin'` (the default) |
| Closest analog | WordPress *themes*; npm-create-* | WordPress *plugins*; VS Code *extensions* |
| Lifecycle hook | `papercusp run` — instantiates a harness from the template | Substrate boot — discovers + mounts global-plugins for active harnesses |

Both share the marketplace pipeline (catalog, signing, retraction, namespaces,
reviews, SBOMs, authors, webhooks). They diverge only in the runtime model:
templates produce instances; plugins extend instances.

## 14.2 Research summary — 8 plugin systems studied

| System | Sandbox | Capability model | Distribution | Hook system | Composition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **VS Code** | Out-of-process extension host + iframe webviews | Manifest `activationEvents` + `contributes`; ~30 surfaces | Bespoke marketplace, ~50k extensions | Typed event API (`vscode.workspace.onDidChange*`) | `extensionDependencies` |
| **WordPress** | None | None (full host privileges) | Bespoke + npm-style; 60k+ plugins | `add_action` / `add_filter` priority numbers | Hook-priority composition |
| **Backstage** | None | DI container `ApiRef` typed services | npm packages, build-time | React context + DI | Plugins ship npm packages with peer-deps |
| **Figma** | iframe + UI iframe + manifest network allowlist | Strongest of survey: manifest declares network domains; iframe enforces | Bespoke marketplace | postMessage RPC | Limited |
| **Obsidian** | None (full Node + DOM) | All-or-nothing at install (cautionary tale) | Bespoke "community plugins" | Vault events + Plugin API | Plugins commonly conflict |
| **Slack apps** | Hosted webhook | OAuth scopes (coarse) | App directory | Event subscriptions | None |
| **Astro / Vite** | None (build-time) | None | npm | Build hooks | Linear pipeline |
| **Probot / Hubot** | Hosted GitHub App / chat bot | Coarse permissions | npm scaffolding | Webhook events | Each app independent |

### The two failure modes to avoid

1. **Obsidian / WordPress's "no sandbox"** — host trivially exploitable by malicious or buggy plugin. Both retroactively bolted on capability prompts.
2. **Backstage's "build-time only"** — installs require rebuild + redeploy. Backstage 2.0 is rebuilding the plugin model around runtime loading.

Papercusp's spec already commits to: iframe sandboxing for v2 UI plugins
(Figma's model), runtime install with capability consent (Chrome Web Store
style), capability strings at the DI boundary (VS Code × Cap'n Proto). This
proposal builds on that foundation.

## 14.3 The four design pillars

### 14.3.1 Reuse the marketplace pipeline; add a `kind` discriminator

`papercusp.json` adds:

```json
{ "kind": "plugin", "name": "@papercupai/cloudflare-pages", "version": "0.1.0", ... }
```

`papercusp publish` is kind-agnostic. The catalog stores `kind` in the package
row. The marketplace site filters at `/marketplace/?kind=template|plugin`
(default both). Search and authors all work without code changes.

`papercusp install` checks the `kind`:
- `template` → registers in `~/.papercusp/registry.json` (already implemented)
- `plugin` → unpacks to `~/.papercusp/global-plugins/<slug>/` (already implemented in plugin-loader); the substrate's plugin-runtime mounts on next `papercusp run`

Both flows go through the same publish + signing + retraction infrastructure.
Operators get the same ops dashboard counts. Authors see "5 templates and
12 plugins published" on their profile.

**Shipped `kind` enum (a third category landed).** The proposal frames the world
as templates vs plugins, but the manifest `kind` enum that shipped is
`plugin | pack | template | snapshot | service | theme | harness`, and the
default is **`plugin`** (not `template` as this proposal originally said). `'pack'`
is a real third distribution category: a **runtime-less code-tool pack** — tools
only, no `ui`/`roles`/`routines`/`actions`, and the runtime must stay `js`. The
loader specially constrains it, rejecting any of those contributions on a pack
(`tool-distribution-granularity-2026-06-05` D-001/D-004). `'snapshot'`,
`'service'`, `'theme'`, and `'harness'` are reserved/dormant — the loader treats
every non-`'pack'` value as a default plugin. The Cupboard's `pack` listing
kind is how these packs surface in the storefront (and `knowledge-pack` is its
sibling install kind for curated pot learnings).

**Plugins ship in one of three runtimes.** Orthogonal to the action handler
model, a plugin declares a `runtime` descriptor in `papercusp.json`. It defaults
to `{ kind: 'js' }`; the other two are `wasm` (a `wasm32-wasip2` component
artifact, loaded via `@papercusp/plugin-loader/wasm`, with a hard
linear-memory budget) and `daemon` (a long-running stdio JSON-RPC peer, loaded
via `@papercusp/plugin-loader/daemon`, with a restart policy). Action-invocation
`concurrency` is `serial` or `parallel` — WASM defaults to serial (mpsc actor),
daemon to parallel. JS plugins keep the in-process model the rest of this page
describes.

### 14.3.2 Plugin lifecycle: install-time consent, harness-time mount

A plugin is **installed once globally** — capability-consent prompt at that
point. Then **mounted at runtime** into every harness instance whose template
`requires` it (or that the user enables via `papercusp plugin enable
cloudflare-pages --harness sheets-clone`).

This matches WordPress's "active plugins per site" + Backstage's "plugins
mounted into the app".

### 14.3.3 New primitive: `actions` (button-shaped, server runtime)

The current SDK has hooks, routes, UI, routines, schema. Missing: a
user-triggered action that the harness UI can surface as a button.

```typescript
export interface ActionDefinition {
  /** Action name. Must match a key registered via ctx.actions.register(). */
  name: string;
  /** Human-readable button label for harness-toolbar etc. */
  label?: string;
  /** Where this action surfaces in the host UI / lifecycle. */
  surfaces?: ('mission-done' | 'harness-toolbar' | 'feature-row' | 'plugin-detail' | string)[];
  /** Capabilities this action additionally requires beyond the plugin's own. */
  capabilities?: Capability[];
  /** JSON-Schema for the params object the handler receives (see §14.3.5). */
  paramsSchema?: Record<string, unknown>;

  /**
   * Server-side handler hints. The actual handler is registered imperatively
   * from the plugin's `init()` via `ctx.actions.register(name, handler)`. The
   * manifest carries no function references — they don't survive serialization.
   */
  serverHandler?: {
    /** Per-invocation timeout in seconds (host enforces via AbortSignal). */
    timeoutSec?: number;
  };

  // Note: actions are strictly USER-CLICKED. There is no `autoOn` field.
  // To auto-fire an action on a substrate event (e.g. `mission.done`), the
  // plugin ships a routine that internally invokes the same handler the
  // action button calls. One trigger registry (routines), one event
  // capability namespace (`events:listen:*`), one audit trail.
}
```

**Actions are server-runtime only.** The proposal originally sketched a
presence-determined dispatch (`serverHandler` → server, `clientHandler` →
iframe, both → hybrid, with a load-time rejection of hybrid manifests). The
shipped `ActionDefinition` has **no `clientHandler` field** — there is no client
or hybrid runtime, no presence-determined dispatch, and no hybrid-rejection code
in the loader or SDK. Every action handler runs in the server runtime (Node, full
DI, capability-checked), registered imperatively from `init()` and dispatched by
the host on a surface event. The forwards-compatibility hook for an iframe
sandbox (§14.9.5) is the `serverHandler` declaration itself — when a client
runtime lands, the manifest gains a sibling declaration without rewriting the
existing server actions.

The `surfaces` enum that shipped is `'mission-done' | 'harness-toolbar' |
'feature-row' | 'plugin-detail'` (plus an open string for forward-compat) — note
`harness-sidebar` from the original sketch is not a defined surface, and
`mission-done`/`plugin-detail` are live additions. There is no `icon` field and
no `defaultTimeoutSec` field on the action; the per-action timeout is set via
`serverHandler.timeoutSec`.

This pattern mirrors VS Code's `contributes.commands` (declarative) +
`commands.registerCommand` (imperative). It avoids the "function in JSON
manifest" trap and keeps a clean migration path to iframe sandboxing.

Three properties make actions worth their own primitive vs reusing
routines/hooks:

1. **They're user-discoverable.** A button in the dashboard. Routines and hooks are invisible to the end user.
2. **They have parameters.** A "Publish" button needs to know the target. JSON-schema → auto-form.
3. **They have execution status.** Async with a progress indicator. Routines fire-and-forget; hooks are passive.

WordPress has admin actions, VS Code has commands, Slack has slash commands,
Backstage has Actions Catalog. We need our equivalent.

### 14.3.4 Capability consent UI at install time

```
Install @papercupai/cloudflare-pages 0.1.0?

You are installing a plugin — it will be enabled into your harness instances
and run alongside the template's logic.

This plugin will be granted:
  ▸ HIGH   secrets:read:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
           — read your Cloudflare API token at deploy time
  ▸ MEDIUM http:fetch:api.cloudflare.com
           — make HTTPS requests to Cloudflare's API
  ▸ LOW    ui:harness-action:publish
           — register a "Publish" button in your harness dashboard
  ▸ LOW    ui:harness-sidebar:cloudflare-publish
           — claim the "cloudflare-publish" sidebar slot
  ▸ LOW    storage:plugin-private
           — store deploy history in plugin-private filesystem

Tier summary (per §10.6.1): 1 high · 1 medium · 3 low

Signed by: @papercupai (verified)
SBOM: no known CVEs (scanned 2026-04-27)

[Install]  [Cancel]
```

Adapted from Chrome Web Store / iOS App Store consent screens, using the
capability tiers we already have (§10.6.1). The first line names what kind of
artifact is being installed (plugin vs template) so users understand the
runtime implications.

### 14.3.5 Capability granularity — per-id everywhere

All UI capabilities are **per-id**, matching the per-id collision-resolution
rule from §10.5. A plugin claiming `ui:dashboard-tab:foo` can mount one tab
named `foo`; mounting `bar` requires a separate `ui:dashboard-tab:bar`
capability.

This makes the consent prompt name what's actually being claimed:

| Capability | What it grants |
|---|---|
| `ui:dashboard-tab:<id>` | One tab in the dashboard tab strip |
| `ui:sidebar-item:<id>` | One sidebar entry in the harness chrome |
| `ui:harness-action:<id>` | One action surface (button, menu item) |
| `ui:harness-route:<slug>` | One full-route mount under `/harness/<slug>` |
| `ui:plugin-config-panel` | Override the auto-generated config form (see §14.3.7) |

The previous coarse `ui:dashboard-tab` (no id) was *proposed* for removal here.
In the shipped SDK, the coarse no-id forms (`ui:dashboard-tab`, `ui:sidebar-item`,
`ui:harness-route`, `ui:tui-pane`) are what landed — the per-id capability
granularity in this section is design intent, not the current `Capability` type.

The shipped UI-surface set is therefore **`react` / `iframe` / `tui-pane`**, and
`ui:tui-pane` is a live capability in addition to the dashboard-tab / sidebar-item
/ harness-route forms above. A `tui-pane` surface contributes a terminal pane
hosted by the pui (`apps/tui`): the pui allocates a managed pane and runs the
surface's declared `command` argv in it (gated by `compute:exec:<command[0]>`,
the same exec-gate as `ctx.spawn`), and the plugin renders its own content
(ratatui or any TUI). The desktop targets (dashboard-tab / harness-route) are
deferred with desktop; the terminal target is what shipped first
(`revive-plugin-system-2026-06-04` D-002).

### 14.3.6 Server-runtime resource isolation

Server-runtime action handlers run as Node code inside the substrate process.
The iframe sandbox (§10.4) does not apply. To prevent one plugin from
degrading the whole harness:

- **Per-action timeout** — `serverHandler.timeoutSec` on the action (default
  60s); substrate cancels via `AbortSignal` threaded through `ctx.signal`.
- **Per-binary subprocess gate** — `compute:exec:<binary>`; see §14.3.6.1 below.
- **Soft heap budget** — substrate polls `process.memoryUsage()` per harness;
  if a plugin's RSS jumps >256 MB above its baseline during a handler call,
  the action is cancelled and the harness logs a budget violation.
- **Postgres connection cap** — plugin's `ctx.db` proxy holds at most one
  connection per concurrent action invocation; long-running queries get the
  same `AbortSignal` as the action.

#### 14.3.6.1 Per-binary subprocess: `compute:exec:<binary>`

The original proposal argued for *no* `process:spawn` capability at all, on the
grounds that common binaries have config flags that spawn other binaries (`git
-c core.fsmonitor=<attacker-binary>` is the canonical example; the same trick
works for `ssh`, `docker`, `npm`, `node`), so a generic spawn gate is unsafe and
a per-(binary, args-pattern) gate would re-implement sudoers.

What shipped is a **per-binary** subprocess capability rather than no spawn at
all: `compute:exec:<binary>` (e.g. `compute:exec:ffmpeg`, with basename
wildcards like `compute:exec:py-*`). A plugin invokes it via
`ctx.spawn(bin, args, { cwd, env, stdin })` and receives `{ stdout, stderr,
code }` after the process exits. The host enforces
`compute:exec:<binary-basename>` against the plugin's declared capabilities
before invoking; `bin` is resolved via PATH and absolute paths are rejected (use
the binary name plus the capability). The named typed wrappers the proposal
sketched (`GitService`, `DockerService`, `execTrustedCommand`, a `TrustedBinary`
enum) do **not** exist in the SDK — the capability gate is the binary-basename
match, and the foot-cannon flags the proposal worried about are an authoring
concern for the plugin, not a substrate-curated allowlist.

The same `compute:exec:<command[0]>` gate is what a `tui-pane` UI surface's
`command` argv runs under (§14.3.5).

### 14.3.7 paramsSchema / configSchema dialect commitment

Every place this proposal says "UI auto-generates a form" needs a precise
contract or it silently degrades to "we ship a generic form, every serious
plugin overrides it" (the WordPress experience).

**Commitments:**

1. **Dialect**: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, **strict subset**:
   - Allowed: `object`, `array`, `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `enum`, `oneOf` for tagged unions
   - Allowed: `format` for `email`, `uri`, `hostname`, `date-time`, `uuid`
   - Disallowed: `$ref` to external URIs (security + offline use); `if/then/else`; `not`; `additionalProperties: <schema>`
   - Disallowed: regex `pattern` containing backreferences (ReDoS class)

2. **Companion `uiSchema`** sibling using RJSF's vocabulary (widgets, hints,
   ordering). Optional. Plugin author writes:
   ```json
   {
     "paramsSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "domain": { "type": "string", "format": "hostname" } } },
     "uiSchema":     { "domain": { "ui:placeholder": "myapp.example.com", "ui:autofocus": true } }
   }
   ```

3. **Escape hatch — `ui:plugin-config-panel` capability**: plugins that need
   full control register their own React component for the config UI. The
   substrate calls into it via the iframe-bridge (or directly in v1 trusted
   server-runtime case).

This is what Backstage and VS Code arrived at after years of "auto-form" debt.
Spec it now.

## 14.4 Worked example: `@papercupai/cloudflare-pages`

```json
// papercusp.json
{
  "kind": "plugin",
  "name": "@papercupai/cloudflare-pages",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "One-click publish your harness's project output to Cloudflare Pages.",
  "papercusp": "^0.1.0",
  "license": "MIT",

  "capabilities": [
    "secrets:read:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN",
    "secrets:read:CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID",
    "http:fetch:api.cloudflare.com",
    "ui:harness-action:publish",
    "ui:harness-sidebar:cloudflare-publish",
    "events:listen:mission.done",
    "storage:plugin-private"
  ],

  "configSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "pages_project":         { "type": "string", "title": "Pages project name", "minLength": 1 },
      "build_dir":             { "type": "string", "title": "Build output dir", "default": "dist" },
      "custom_domain":         { "type": "string", "format": "hostname", "title": "Custom domain (optional)" },
      "auto_publish_on_done":  { "type": "boolean", "title": "Auto-publish on mission complete", "default": false }
    },
    "required": ["pages_project"]
  },
  "uiSchema": {
    "pages_project": { "ui:placeholder": "myapp" },
    "custom_domain": { "ui:placeholder": "myapp.example.com" }
  },

  "actions": [
    {
      "name": "publish",
      "label": "Publish to Cloudflare Pages",
      "surfaces": ["harness-toolbar", "mission-done"],
      "capabilities": ["secrets:read:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "http:fetch:api.cloudflare.com"],
      "serverHandler": { "timeoutSec": 120 }
    }
  ],

  "routines": [
    {
      "name": "auto-publish-on-done",
      "trigger": { "kind": "event", "event": "mission.done" },
      "targetAction": "publish",
      "enabledIfConfig": "auto_publish_on_done"
    }
  ]
}
```

```typescript
// index.ts
import type { Plugin, PapercuspContext } from '@papercusp/plugin-sdk';

async function publishHandler(ctx: PapercuspContext, params: unknown) {
  const token = await ctx.api.secrets.read('CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN');
  const accountId = await ctx.api.secrets.read('CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID');
  const projectName = ctx.config.pages_project;
  const buildDir = join(ctx.projectDir, ctx.config.build_dir ?? 'dist');

  // Honour the AbortSignal from the substrate (timeout / user-cancel)
  const r = await ctx.api.fetch(`https://api.cloudflare.com/...`, {
    signal: ctx.signal,
    /* ... */
  });

  // Write to the per-action audit log via context
  await ctx.audit('publish.success', { url: `https://${projectName}.pages.dev` });

  return { ok: true, result: { url: `https://${projectName}.pages.dev` } };
}

export default {
  name: '@papercupai/cloudflare-pages',
  version: '0.1.0',
  papercusp: '^0.1.0',
  capabilities: [...],
  configSchema: {...},
  actions: [{ name: 'publish', /* ... */ serverHandler: { timeoutSec: 120 } }],

  init(ctx) {
    // Imperative registration — no function in the manifest.
    ctx.actions.register('publish', publishHandler);
  },
} satisfies Plugin;
```

User flow:
1. `papercusp install @papercupai/cloudflare-pages` → consent screen → installed globally
2. `papercusp plugin enable cloudflare-pages --harness sheets-clone` → form for `pages_project`, etc.
3. User goes to `/harness/sheets-clone` → "Publish to Cloudflare Pages" button on the harness toolbar
4. Click → progress modal → success URL

For auto-publish on mission complete: the routine declared in the manifest
fires when the substrate emits `mission.done`. The routine handler invokes the
same `publishHandler` function the action button does — single code path,
single audit trail.

`papercup-coding`'s template manifest just adds:

```json
{ "recommends": ["@papercupai/cloudflare-pages@^0.1"] }
```

The install flow then suggests "papercup-coding works well with cloudflare-pages
— install it too?" but doesn't force.

## 14.5 Existing tab classification — what should be plugin vs core?

The current papercusp dashboard has **8 tabs**: proposals, dashboard, summary,
docs, vscode, pi, insights, config. Each needs a classification: keep in core,
or extract to a plugin?

The principle: **a tab is core if every harness — coding, research-org,
content-pipeline, marketing-bot, anything — would benefit from it**. A tab is
a plugin if it's specific to one template family or external integration.

| Tab | Today's content | Recommended | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dashboard** | Feature queue, agents, logs, issues — the main canvas | **CORE** | This IS the harness UI. Every harness has features+agents+logs. Plugins contribute INTO it via `dashboardTabs`/`sidebarItems`. If this were a plugin, harnesses with no plugins would have nothing to show. |
| **summary** | High-level changelog of what's been built | **CORE** | Generic across all templates. A research-org harness wants "what got researched"; a content-pipeline wants "what got published"; coding wants "what features shipped". Same primitive. |
| **insights** | Features count, cost, tokens, iterations | **CORE** | Universal harness metrics. Every harness pays for tokens; every harness has iterations. |
| **config** | Per-instance configuration | **CORE** | Every harness needs config. Plugins contribute their own config sections via `configSchema`. |
| **proposals** | AI-generated scope expansion suggestions for the SPEC.md | **CORE for v1**, defer extraction | See §14.6 — proposals isn't a UI tab extraction, it's an authorization-model question. |
| **docs** | iframe of project docs (fumadocs on :4325) | **PLUGIN** (`@papercupai/fumadocs`) | Optional integration with an external docs server. Templates that don't generate docs shouldn't see this tab. |
| **vscode** | iframe of code-server on the project dir | **RETIRED plugin** (was `@papercupai/vscode-server`) | Retired 2026-07-07 with the bundled code-server surface. Keep this as historical context for why IDE tabs belong outside core. |
| **pi** | iframe of the pi (omp) interactive coding agent | **PLUGIN** (`@papercupai/pi-companion`) | Pi is one specific external tool. Would be like baking "ChatGPT side panel" into Slack. |

### Where this proposal disagrees with the maintainer's initial take

The maintainer suggested:
- Core: pi, insights, Config
- Plugins: proposals, dashboard, summary, docs, vscode

This proposal disagrees on three of them:

1. **`dashboard` should stay CORE, not become a plugin.** The dashboard is the
   composition surface — it's where plugins' actions and tabs render. Making it
   a plugin would mean "harness with no plugins = empty UI" which breaks the
   first-run experience and the "core works without plugins" guarantee.
2. **`summary` should stay CORE.** Every harness benefits from "what got done";
   the implementation is template-agnostic (read features+goals from state,
   render a timeline). Pulling it into a plugin would force every template
   author to either reimplement it or depend on the same plugin (a tax on
   adoption).
3. **`pi` should be a PLUGIN, not core.** Pi/omp is one specific external tool;
   not all harnesses use it. Treating it as core would tie papercusp to one
   external tool.

**The dashboard nuance**: the dashboard *chrome* (tab strip, panel layout,
action surfaces) stays core. The dashboard's *primary panel* (feature queue
for coding ≠ briefing pipeline for research-org) is contributed by the active
template via a `defaultDashboardPanel` UI contribution. Templates ship their
own dashboard panel; the chrome stays core.

## 14.6 Migration plan — porting tabs to plugins

The migration is straightforward because each tab is already an isolated React
component in `apps/papercusp/app/harness/`. Each plugin extraction is:

1. Move the component file into `libs/papercusp-marketplace/seeds/papercupai/<plugin-name>/src/`
2. Wrap it in a `Plugin` export with appropriate per-id capabilities
3. Replace the inline `activePanel === 'X'` render with a `dashboardTabs` contribution
4. Publish via the seed-publish pipeline (service token model)
5. Add to `papercup-coding`'s `recommends:` so existing users get it on install

Per-tab effort estimate (post-Phase-P2):

| Tab → Plugin | Lines | Capabilities | Est | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vscode` → `@papercupai/vscode-server` | ~10 (iframe) | `ui:harness-tab:vscode` + config `code_server_url` | 30 min | **Retired 2026-07-07** |
| `docs` → `@papercupai/fumadocs` | ~10 (iframe) | `ui:harness-tab:docs` + config `docs_url` | 30 min | P7 |
| `pi` → `@papercupai/pi-companion` | ~150 (PiPanel) | `ui:harness-tab:pi` + typed-services for child-process needs | 1.5h | P7 |
| `proposals` → `@papercupai/scope-proposals` | substrate-protocol change | New: plugin authorization to mutate harness-canonical state | DEFERRED to v1.5 | See note |

**Why proposals is deferred to v1.5**: proposals isn't a UI panel extraction.
The blocker is **the write side** — today `apply_proposal_to_spec` is
substrate code mutating substrate-canonical state (SPEC.md, the goals tree).
For proposals to live in a plugin, the substrate has to authorize a plugin to
mutate harness-canonical state, which is a real authorization-model question
(not "let plugins call substrate functions" — those exist via the DI proxy —
but "let plugins overwrite the harness contract"). Designing that
authorization model is its own milestone; until then, proposals stays core.

Total v1 migration effort (vscode + docs + pi): ~2.5h of straightforward
refactoring once the action + tab plugin primitives are in place.

The migration is **non-breaking** because:
- Each tab keeps its component code, just relocates
- The dashboard chrome already has a generic `dashboardTabs` slot
- Plugins are loaded at substrate boot; existing harnesses see them on next `papercusp run`
- Templates that haven't been republished still work (they just don't get the new tabs until users explicitly install the plugins)

## 14.7 Implementation roadmap

Order matters; later items depend on earlier.

**Status — 2026-04-27**: P1 → P8 shipped + operator dashboards for
`audit.action_executions` (drill-down + webhooks) and plugin grants
(`granted-capabilities.json` + `extended-grants.json` with revoke). **Seven** in-tree reference plugins (`@papercupai/{vscode-server,
cloudflare-pages,pi-coding,fumadocs,slack-notifier,postgres-manager,
notion-export}`) published to the local marketplace; full publish → catalog
→ install → enable → lockfile round-trip verified end-to-end with the
service-token CI flow. Drill-down drawer has **Detail** + **History** tabs +
a **Retry** button (re-invokes via the substrate CLI, mirrors the result back
into `audit.action_executions`) + a **diagnose→remediate** affordance that
surfaces a "revoke grants for this plugin" shortcut when an error message
looks capability-related. Per-plugin audit page at
`/papercusp-marketplace-ops/plugins/<slug>` aggregates every audit row across
all action names with per-action filter chips. Top-of-page sticky nav links
the four sections (Stats / Recent / Plugin grants / Action failures) with a
red-pill count when there are recent failures. Webhook subscriptions are managed inline (operator-token-gated; create with
event-type chips, disable/enable/delete per row, expandable per-row delivery
log). `papercusp lock {check,upgrade-all,prune}` closes the lockfile-hygiene
loop on the CLI; `lock prune` cascades transitive-orphan removal. Capability-
aware install diff shows `+added` / `-removed` per cap before the consent
prompt fires when there's a prior grant. Per-harness audit page mirrors the
per-plugin one — drill in from the harness column in the grants table to see
every action invocation across all plugins on that harness. Both the per-
harness and per-plugin pages show a cross-pivot grants table linking back to
the other axis. History tab surfaces a per-row "vs prior" diff hint (same /
+N / -M / ~K) so flaky-but-equivalent vs flaky-and-different is visible at a
glance. Webhook deliveries sub-table is sortable by status / attempt / ts and
gains a per-row replay button that resets a delivery to attempt 0. The drawer
is deep-linkable via `?drawer=<auditId>`; back/forward syncs the open state
naturally. Grants table supports multi-select + bulk-revoke and renders
capability pills color-coded by tier (high=red, medium=amber, low=grey).
Recent-action-failures table is now substring-filterable by harness, plugin,
or error message. Persistent operator audit log
(`audit.operator_actions`) records every operator-token-gated mutation and
surfaces in a new dashboard panel with substring filtering. Grants table
supports tier filter chips (high/medium/low) so operators can isolate the
dangerous grants. Audit log + grants table both have CSV export for offline
records. Webhook subscriptions can rotate their HMAC secret with a one-shot
reveal modal. Marketplace Ed25519 signing key has an inspect + rotate surface
that archives the old key (timestamped) and continues serving signatures
already minted against archived keys. Test coverage: 27 plugin-loader action tests + 7 hot-reload + 12
lockfile + 7 lock-resolve + 15 consent + 7 plugin-cli + 9 grants = **84
passing**.
Bonus operator surfaces: `papercusp plugin invoke <slug> <action>`,
`papercusp plugin watch <slug>`, `papercusp upgrade-pin <slug>`,
marketplace-ops Action-executions card + Recent-action-failures table +
per-row drill-down drawer, a 30-second poller that emits `action.failed` /
`action.timeout` webhook deliveries from `audit.action_executions`, and a
**Plugin grants** card + per-harness table with revoke + sticky "extended
to all" un-stick.

Live state: `audit.action_executions` migration applied to the running
`papercusp` Postgres DB (incl. `webhook_emitted_at` column for scanner

server-side (no token needed; operator filesystem is the boundary).

### Phase P1 — Add `kind` to publishes (~2h, completely additive) ✅ shipped

- Schema: `ALTER TABLE packages ADD COLUMN kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'template'`
- Server: read `manifest.kind` on publish, default to `'template'`, store in DB + Typesense
- Marketplace site: `/marketplace/?kind=plugin` filter; type pill on cards (UI affordance left to design — kind in the data, layout decision deferred)
- E2E test: `?kind=` query parameter
- Vocabulary updates (already shipped)

### Phase P2 — Action primitive in the plugin SDK (~3h) ✅ shipped

- Add `ActionDefinition` to `@papercusp/plugin-sdk` (server-handler shape — `serverHandler` only; no `clientHandler`/hybrid runtime)
- Add `actions` field to `Plugin` interface
- Add `ctx.actions.register(name, handler)` to the `PapercuspContext`
- Loader collects all installed plugins' actions on harness start
- Substrate API endpoint: `POST /api/harness/:slug/actions/:plugin-name/:action-name` — runs handler with `AbortSignal`, captures result, writes to audit
- Capability check at proxy level (already implemented in plugin-loader)
- **Test coverage in `packages/papercusp-plugin-loader/src/`**:
  - registering an action name that wasn't declared in the manifest → reject
  - registering the same action twice → reject
  - registering after `init()` returns → reject
- Surface in harness UI via existing slots

### Phase P3 — Plugin install/enable CLI commands (~2h) ✅ shipped

- `papercusp install` already works for plugins (kind=plugin → `~/.papercusp/global-plugins/`)
- `papercusp plugin list` — show installed + enabled-for-harness map
- `papercusp plugin enable <slug> [--harness <slug>]` — interactive form per `configSchema` + `uiSchema`
- `papercusp plugin disable <slug> [--harness <slug>]`
- `papercusp plugin config <slug> [--harness <slug>]` — re-edit
- **Bonus**: `papercusp plugin invoke <slug> <action> [--params '<json>'] [--dry-run]` — operator-facing manual action trigger; reads per-harness config, runs through the registry's invoke pipeline (timeout + idempotency + audit), exits 5 on `ok=false`.

### Phase P3.5 — `papercusp.lock` per-instance lockfile (~3h) ✅ shipped

- New file: `~/.papercusp/harnesses/<slug>/papercusp.lock`
- Records `{ plugin, version, granted-caps-hash }` per enabled plugin + transitive `requires`
- Recommends entries are **not** in the lockfile until the user accepts them
- `papercusp run` reads the lockfile; if a referenced plugin is missing locally, fail loud with `papercusp install --from-lock` suggestion
- New CLI: `papercusp install --from-lock` rehydrates plugins from the lockfile
- Retraction interaction (see §14.9 below)
- **Bonus**: `papercusp upgrade-pin <slug> [--harness <slug>]` — re-pins a withdrawn/quarantined plugin to its latest active version. Closes the loop on the lockfile error message that suggests this command.

### Phase P4 — Plugin install consent UI (~3h) ✅ shipped

- `papercusp install` shows the capability consent screen before downloading the tarball
- `--accept-capabilities` flag for non-interactive (CI)
- `~/.papercusp/granted-capabilities.json` records approvals — see §14.9 grant scope
- Re-prompt on update if new high-tier capabilities appear
- The "extend to other harnesses" sticky affordance from §14.9

### Phase P4.5 — Action handler failure semantics (~2h) ✅ shipped

- Per-action timeout enforced via `AbortSignal` (default 60s, override via `serverHandler.timeoutSec`)
- Idempotency keys derived from `(harness-slug, action-name, trigger-source-id)` so substrate restarts mid-action don't double-publish
- New table `audit.action_executions { id, harness_slug, plugin_name, action_name, started_at, completed_at, status, error_msg, trigger_source }` mirroring existing `audit.hook_executions`
- Failure UX: persistent audit row + a banner on the action's surface
- Routine that failed-action: backoff per spec §9 (existing routine retry policy applies)

### Phase P5 — `@papercupai/vscode-server` reference plugin (~1h) ✅ shipped, retired 2026-07-07

**Pilot the smallest existing tab first**, so the new primitives get exercised
against real production code before we build greenfield on top. This pilot was
later removed with the bundled code-server surface; the plugin extraction
lesson remains, but the package is no longer shipped.

- Migrate vscode iframe (~10 LOC) into a plugin
- Capability: `ui:harness-tab:vscode` + config `code_server_url`
- No server runtime, no secrets, no network — purest possible plugin
- Validates the action + tab + config primitives end-to-end

### Phase P6 — `@papercupai/cloudflare-pages` reference plugin (~3h) ✅ shipped

- First "real" plugin: secrets + http + storage + server-runtime action + routine
- Built on validated P5 primitives
- Published via the seed-publish pipeline (existing service token model)

### Phase P7 — Migrate `pi` and `docs` tabs (~2h) ✅ plugins shipped, cutover gated

- Per-tab effort breakdown in §14.6
- `proposals` is deferred to v1.5 (see §14.6 note)
- Cutover from legacy hard-coded tabs to the plugin-mounted ones is gated by `PAPERCUSP_TABS_FROM_PLUGINS=1` to avoid colliding with concurrent harness-UI rewrites; flag flip is operator-controlled.

### Phase P8 — Hot-reload for plugin development (~3h, optional) ✅ shipped (with caveat)

- `HotReloader` class in `packages/papercusp-plugin-loader/src/hot-reload.ts` watches plugin dirs (recursive), debounces bursts, emits `changed` + `reloaded` + `error` events.
- CLI surface: `papercusp plugin watch <slug> [--src <dir>]` — useful for plugin authors iterating in-tree.
- **Caveat**: under `tsx` the ESM cache isn't invalidated by query-string bust, so the `reloaded` event fires with the original module contents. The `changed` event still fires correctly and is the right signal for a "restart needed" workflow. Full content-fresh hot-reload would require either spawning a fresh tsx child per reload or using `tsx watch` to restart the harness — left for v1.5.

### Phase P9+ — More reference plugins, marketplace polish

- `@papercupai/slack-notifier`, `@papercupai/postgres-manager`, `@papercupai/notion-export`
- Plugin-specific detail-page sections (capabilities listed prominently)

**Total Phase P1-P7 estimate: ~16-20 hours** to a working "one-click publish"
loop with three core tabs migrated to plugins.

## 14.8 Tradeoffs

- **vs. Backstage's build-time-only:** we pay for runtime loading with the iframe sandbox v2 work and per-instance config UI. Worth it — the marketplace pitch needs runtime install.
- **vs. WordPress's full-trust plugins:** we pay for the capability system with manifest verbosity and consent friction. Worth it — we won't have an Obsidian-style retroactive cleanup.
- **vs. VS Code's command system:** we collapse "commands" + "API contributions" into one `actions` primitive. VS Code distinguishes because their plugins do many non-action things (language servers, decorations, etc). Our plugins are smaller-surface; one primitive suffices.
- **vs. Slack's hosted apps:** we run plugins **on the user's substrate**, not on our infrastructure. The capability sandbox makes this safe-ish; it also means plugins can do things hosted ones can't (read project files, work offline).
- **`actions` vs reusing `routines`:** distinct surfaces, single trigger registry. Actions = user-clicked buttons (with parameters, status UI). Routines = scheduled/event-fired (cron, webhook, substrate event). A routine that targets an action (`targetAction: 'publish'`) is the same code path as the user-clicked action, with `trigger-source` differing in the audit row.
- **No `process:spawn` capability in v1:** plugins that need subprocess access use typed substrate services or contribute upstream. Trade flexibility for safety; lift in v1.5 if proven necessary.

## 14.9 Resolved decisions

These were open questions in the v1 draft and resolved through review.

### 14.9.1 Plugin scope: per-machine install + per-harness enable

Plugins are installed once globally (`papercusp install <slug>`). They're
enabled per harness instance via `papercusp plugin enable`. This matches every
comparable system (VS Code, WordPress active-plugins-per-site, Backstage).

### 14.9.2 Granted-capabilities scope: per-(plugin, version, harness-slug) with sticky extension

The decision: **strict per-(plugin, version, harness-slug)** as the default.
**Sticky "extend to other harnesses" affordance at second-use**.

Concrete consent flow:

1. **First grant** (e.g. `secrets:read:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` for harness
   `sheets-clone`): one prompt, granted for `sheets-clone` only. Recorded in
   `granted-capabilities.json` as `{plugin: 'cloudflare-pages', version: '0.1.0', harness: 'sheets-clone', cap: 'secrets:read:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN'}`.

2. **Second grant of the same cap from a different harness** (e.g. enabling
   the plugin on `random-research-spike`): the prompt now offers two buttons:
   - **Grant for this harness only** — adds `harness: 'random-research-spike'` row
   - **Grant for all current and future harnesses on this machine** — wildcards the harness slug (`harness: '*'`); future harnesses re-evaluate without re-prompting

3. **Update with new capability** (e.g. plugin v0.2.0 adds
   `secrets:read:CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_API_TOKEN`): per §10.8 update flow, prompt
   for the new capability only; existing grants survive.

This gives strict isolation by default (no silent cross-harness leakage), one
prompt for the common case (one-harness-per-plugin), and an explicit
opt-in for the convenience case.

Three alternatives considered + rejected:
- **Uniform per-machine** (simplest, every plugin marketplace does it) — accepts that secrets installed for harness A are usable by harness B on the same box.
- **Uniform per-(plugin, version, harness-slug)** with a "remember for all" checkbox at first prompt — one consent surface; the high-cost case is the explicit unchecked default.
- **Tier-graded scope** (low per-machine, medium per-(machine, plugin, version), high per-(machine, plugin, version, harness-slug)) — three different scope semantics is too much complexity to ship without two consent surfaces designed first.

The chosen path balances safety (strict default) and friction (one-prompt
common case) without inventing new prompt surfaces.

### 14.9.3 Default dashboard panel ownership

Templates contribute their default dashboard panel via a
`defaultDashboardPanel` UI contribution in the template's manifest. Render
order: template's panel first; plugins' tabs appended.

### 14.9.4 First-party vs community parity

`@papercupai/*` plugins get prominence (verified badge, default ranking) but
no extra capabilities. Same security model for everyone.

### 14.9.5 Forwards-compatibility with iframe sandbox v2

The action handler's runtime is **explicit in the manifest** via the
`serverHandler` declaration (§14.3.3). Actions are server-runtime only today;
when an iframe-sandboxed client runtime lands, the manifest gains a sibling
declaration and existing server actions don't get rewritten — the loader
resolves to the right execution path based on what's in the manifest.

### 14.9.6 Lockfile retraction interaction

Three retraction states map to three lockfile behaviors:

| State | Author intent | Lockfile reaction |
|---|---|---|
| `deprecated` | "still works, prefer X going forward" | Warn at `papercusp run`, proceed normally |
| `withdrawn` | "I removed this, but please don't break grandfathered installs" | Warn loud at `papercusp run`, require `--allow-withdrawn` flag to actually run |
| `quarantined` | "this version is actively unsafe — security issue or supply-chain compromise" | Refuse to run, force `papercusp upgrade-pin <plugin>` to bump to next non-retracted version |

Same rules apply to `recommends` entries: a recommends pointing at a
quarantined plugin is **stripped from the suggestion UI entirely** (not shown
with a warning).

### 14.9.7 Lockfile transitivity

The rule: **every line in the lockfile is something the user explicitly chose
to be in their world**.

- **Hard `requires`** are pinned transitively in the lockfile (npm/cargo
  behavior). The plugin author tested against a specific dep version;
  surprises are bugs.
- **`recommends` are NOT in the lockfile until the user accepts them.** Once
  accepted, they enter the lockfile and pin transitively from then on (the
  recommended plugin's own `requires` get pinned).
- An un-accepted `recommends` showing up after a template version bump
  re-prompts but doesn't pin until acceptance.

This invariant makes lockfiles legible to humans, which matters more for a
marketplace than for npm.

### 14.9.8 `recommends` UX touch-points

- **CLI**: `papercusp install <template>` shows the recommends list with `--with-recommends` (default off) and `--no-recommends` flags
- **Web admin**: modal at template-install completion with checkboxes
- **Re-evaluation**: on `papercusp run` if the lockfile shows recommends mismatching the current template version, prompt; on a template version bump, the install flow re-shows the recommends diff
- **Persisted state**: track which recommends were "skipped" so we don't keep re-asking (`~/.papercusp/skipped-recommends.json`)

## 14.10 Plugin → plugin dependencies

Both `requires` and `recommends` are valid at **both** template and plugin
manifest levels:

```json
// In a plugin's papercusp.json
{
  "kind": "plugin",
  "name": "@papercupai/cloudflare-pages-history",
  "requires": ["@papercupai/cloudflare-pages@^0.1"]
}
```

Resolution at install time:

1. Substrate computes the transitive closure of `requires`
2. Substrate prompts user for capability consent for ALL plugins in the closure
3. If any plugin in the closure is `quarantined`, refuse install; if any is `withdrawn`, require explicit override
4. On install, all transitive `requires` enter the lockfile (per §14.9.7)
5. `recommends` from the leaf packages are surfaced separately (per §14.9.8) and not pinned until accepted

This matches VS Code's `extensionDependencies` + `extensionPack` semantics.
The retraction-aware install flow (§14.9.6) applies uniformly to all plugins
in the closure.
